description: Collect public web data with one HashScraper bot (find the worker — or, for a bot made by a member, the public_bot slug — with catalog first) and return the rows — e.g. a Coupang product page's price, 50 Naver blog posts for a keyword, reviews, map places. Uses only the daily free credits unless use_credits=true. The first paid use needs the user's agreement to the data terms (accept_terms). It waits up to wait_seconds; if the bot is still collecting it returns a dataset id — call fetch later instead of running again.

accept_terms.description: The data terms version the user was shown and clearly agreed to (e.g. "v0.2"). Only set it after the user agrees; never agree for the user.

csv_path.description: Absolute path ending in .csv. Saves ALL rows to this file (UTF-8 with BOM, opens in Excel) instead of returning them in the answer.

inputs.description: Bot inputs: keys are "param1"… or the input name / English name from catalog; values are text (several URLs or keywords: an array or one per line). Omitted inputs use the bot's saved settings.

max_rows.description: Return at most this many rows in the answer (default 100). The summary always shows the total.

public_bot.description: Slug of a bot made by a HashScraper member, from the "made by members" part of catalog, e.g. "shopprice1". It is added to the user's account and run with the price shown there (credits per row, charged to the user; daily free credits first). Pass exactly one of worker or public_bot.

use_credits.description: Set true only if the user wants to spend their own credits after today's free credits are used up.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the collection in this call (default 45, max 55). If it is not finished, the answer says to call fetch later.

worker.description: Worker name of a built-in bot from catalog, e.g. "DemoCoupangDetailWorker". Pass exactly one of worker or public_bot.

name: run
title: Collect data with a bot
